Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Issue: Real FILES() cardinalities in the StarRocks FE. Three designs were written to /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/files-cardinality-surgical.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/files-cardinality-robust.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/files-cardinality-upstream.md. Their structured summaries: [
 {
  "summary": "Surgical FE-only fix for issue 3: replace the hard-coded `setOutputRowCount(1)` in `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (FE StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676) with rows = sum(listed file bytes) / sum(getTypeSize of the inferred schema) for `TableFunctionTable` scans, behind a mutable FE config `files_query_estimate_row_count` (default on). Both inputs already exist on the FE before the optimizer runs (TableFunctionTable.java:587-624 file sizes at :611, schema from the get_file_schema RPC at :688-730); no proto or CN change. On SF1000 the estimate lands within 0.2x-6x of the footer counts for all 8 tables (lineitem 1.23e9 vs 6.0e9, orders 5.7e8 vs 1.5e9, partsupp 1.05e9 vs 8e8, customer 1.12e8 vs 1.5e8, part 4.5e7 vs 2e8, supplier 8.6e6 vs 1e7, nation 56 vs 25, region 30 vs 5) and preserves the fact-vs-dimension ordering. It fixes C1 (card_all_one for 22/22 plans) and the P3 class where a tiny dimension is shuffled/broadcast the wrong way (q02, q11, q22). Hand computation of the FE cost model says it does NOT un-break the six 1-CN failures and may flip q03/q12 (possibly q07/q10) at 1 CN from streaming lineitem/orders to hash-partitioning them, because HashJoinCostModel's broadcast probe-cache penalty (up to 12x vs 3x) makes the FE shuffle any join whose build exceeds ~1e7 estimated rows. Hence the knob and an EXPLAIN COSTS survey (minutes, translate-only CN) as the gate before any SF1000 sweep. Full design with code excerpts at /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/files-cardinality-surgical.md.",
  "mechanism": "In `computeFileScanNode`, keep every column statistic UNKNOWN, but set outputRowCount = max(1, bytes/width) where bytes = sum of `TBrokerFileStatus.size` over `TableFunctionTable.loadFileList()` (non-dir entries; filled by the FE's own globList at TableFunctionTable.java:587-624) and width = sum of `Column.getType().getTypeSize()` over `getFullSchema()` (PrimitiveType.java:343-403: INT/DATE/DECIMAL32 4, BIGINT/DECIMAL64 8, DECIMAL128 16, VARCHAR 16). Guards: `Config.files_query_estimate_row_count` off -> 1; table not a TableFunctionTable (external FileTable via visitLogicalFileScan/visitPhysicalFileScan) -> 1; list_files_only -> 1. Also set `setTableRowCountMayInaccurate(true)` (inert: every consumer is already short-circuited by unknown column stats). The estimator is self-consistent with the CBO because Statistics.getOutputSize (Statistics.java:97-99) prices unknown columns with the same getTypeSize, so the estimated bytes of a full scan equal the on-disk bytes. Downstream, predicates on unknown columns keep their fixed coefficients (range 0.5 per conjunct, numeric equality 0.5, string equality 1.0, IN 0.5, col<col 0.5, other 0.25) and equi-joins on unknown keys estimate max(L,R) (StatisticsCalculator.java:1219-1240). Under the SF1000 case (q05 exch 9): build orders_f x customer est 1.42e8 rows / 1.7 GB, probe lineitem 1.23e9 rows / 34.5 GB; broadcast cost 135e9 vs shuffle 95e9 (network counted) or 40e9 (single registered node) because P_b = ln(1.42e8/1e5) = 7.26 vs P_s ~1 (HashJoinCostModel.java:134-156), so lineitem stays under a HASH_PARTITIONED sink and the six still fail on 1 CN. Under the 15 passing queries: builds below ~3e5 rows (region, nation, filtered supplier) are broadcast, so q02's 800M-row partsupp shuffles on n_regionkey (38.5 of ~45 GB nixl at 4 CN, 13.1 GB parked at 1 CN) and q11's supplier shuffle disappear; q22's 1.5e9-row orders broadcast (18.56 GB nixl) exceeds the 2 GiB penalty and becomes a shuffle or a RIGHT ANTI on the customer side; q03/q10/q12/q14/q19 stay PARTITIONED at 4 CN (guard + probe term), and at 1 CN q03 (lineitem_f 3.23e9 rows x 24 B = 77.6 GB) and q12 (orders 1.5e9 x 24 B = 36 GB) are predicted to flip from streaming to parking. Delivered as `experimental/starrocks/patches/files-query-row-estimate.patch` applied by `scripts/apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, rebuilt with `pixi run -e fe fe-build`; togglable at runtime via ADMIN SET FRONTEND CONFIG for A/B on one FE.",

Pass: card_all_one=False for all 22 with FileScanNode cardinalities 1,230,652,806 / 569,291,596 / 1,052,185,030 / 112,102,183 / 45,394,799 / 8,585,358 / 56 / 30; q02 join 31 and q11 join 5 broadcast region/nation; q22 join 11 no longer broadcasts orders; no 'hash join type is unsupported' or MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK refusal in the CN log for the 15 passing queries (with cbo_cte_reuse=false); every 1-CN BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flip listed with the bytes it will park. Golden files under benchmarks/tpch/plans/.",
   "Acceptance B (SF1000, orchestrator-run, one arm at a time, only after A is clean): 1-CN and 4-CN run-queries.sh sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six with the campaign configuration and cbo_cte_reuse=false; record plan shapes (explain_summary.py), per-exchange actual rows (card_compare.py), warm medians vs results.md, oracle compares (MATCH set unchanged; known decimal diffs unchanged); 4 CN nixl GB per run for q02 (43.6-45.7 -> ~8), q11 (0.40 -> ~0), q22 (18.56 -> 0.3-4.5), q03/q12 unchanged; 1 CN [gpu_pool] peak and export_packed time for q03/q12; the six still fail (expected), time-to-fail owned by fix 1."

  "predicted_effect": "Deterministic: card_all_one goes from 22/22 to 0/22 plans; FileScanNode cardinalities within 0.2x-6x of footer counts (measured inputs: du -sb bytes and metadata.json row counts, FE type widths). Inference from the FE cost code (verified by acceptance test A): 4 CN data movement per run q02 ~45 GB -> ~8 GB (four 800M-row partsupp shuffles on n_regionkey/s_nationkey replaced by region/nation broadcasts), q22 18.56 GB -> 0.3-4.5 GB (orders no longer broadcast; build on ~6e6 customers if RIGHT ANTI is chosen, HASH_JOIN(15) 0.516 s per CN plausibly drops 0.3-0.4 s of the 831 ms), q11 0.40 GB -> ~0; q03 (60.34 GB), q07 (69.01), q10 (48.04), q12 (23.47) unchanged because their builds are >= 1e7 estimated rows and the probe-cache term keeps them PARTITIONED (contrary to the report's P3 hope for q12/q19). 1 CN: the six (q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21) still OOM (lineitem stays under a HASH_PARTITIONED sink: broadcast 135e9 vs shuffle 95e9/40e9 for q05 exch 9); q03 predicted to park lineitem_f 77.6 GB (+~1.2 s of export_packed at the measured 63 GB/s) and q12 to park orders 36 GB (+~0.6 s) instead of streaming them; q07/q10 at risk; q19/q22 neutral-to-better; q01/q06/q13/q14/q15/q20 unchanged. No effect on P4's 120-270 ms head. This fix is the prerequisite for the P5 semi/anti flips and for any stats-aware plan-shape work; it does not deliver any of the six on 1 CN, so fix 4 remains mandatory.",
  "risks": [

Mitigation: the mutable knob; run fix 2 first; the real fix is a separate FE patch neutralising the probe penalty for this deployment (out of scope, robust design).",

Land the one-arm translator change (report item 5) first or record the refusals.",

Mitigation: SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse = false (SessionVariable.java:1505-1506 -> CTEContext.needInline returns true).",

Decisions studied hinge on >=10x ratios or thresholds far from the estimates; a many-string fact table joined to a one-row dimension is the case to watch.",

Acceptance B: two SF1000 sweeps of ~20-30 minutes wall each, orchestrator-run. Total roughly 1-2 engineer-days excluding build wall time.",
  "dependencies": [

  "summary": "Give the StarRocks FE real FILES() statistics by extending the schema RPC the CN already answers from parquet footers (per-file num_rows, file_size, per-column null_count/min/max in a new repeated PFileStatistics field of PGetFileSchemaResult), store them on the per-statement TableFunctionTable, and have StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode emit the exact row count plus finite column ranges (bytes/row-width fallback flagged tableRowCountMayInaccurate when the CN sends nothing). Because hand-computation of the FE cost code shows statistics alone still shuffle lineitem at 1 CN (zero single-node shuffle network cost, x1000 penalty above the 2 GiB exec_mem_limit, 12x-vs-3x broadcast probe penalty), the design pairs them with four SET GLOBAL defaults (exec_mem_limit 64 GiB, enable_local_shuffle_agg=false, broadcast_row_limit 2e9, cbo_cte_reuse=false) and one flag-gated 4-line cost change (enable_sirius_gpu_join_cost caps the broadcast probe penalty at the shuffle cap). Mutable FE config files_query_statistics_mode = off|rows|rows_ranges|rows_ranges_ndv is the kill switch and the NDV heuristic is a separate mode. Full design with cost arithmetic, tests, failure modes and code excerpts: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/files-cardinality-robust.md",
  "mechanism": "Root cause (measured): StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676 sets outputRowCount=1 and every column ColumnStatistic.unknown() for FILES() scans, reached via visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan (:374-376); with all sides at 1 row the CBO's fragment cut is arithmetic on widths and node count (HashJoinCostModel.java:115-127, CostModel.java:419-441), the broadcast guard never fires (EnforceAndCostTask.java:324-325 needs right rows > 15M), CTE inlining always wins and semi/anti joins never commute. Row counts already exist: TBrokerFileStatus.size per file on the FE (TableFunctionTable.java:606-613) and the parquet footer the CN already parses for the schema RPC (file_schema.rs:14-27; parquet-rs 59.2.0 FileMetaData::num_rows, ColumnChunkMetaData::statistics). Part A: proto patch adds PFileColumnStatistics{col_name,null_count,min,max,uncompressed_bytes,distinct_count}, PFileStatistics{path,num_rows,file_size,columns} and `repeated PFileStatistics file_statistics = 3` to PGetFileSchemaResult (internal_service.proto:647-650; all optional so version skew degrades, never fails). CN: parquet_file_schema/parquet_files_schema return the footer statistics alongside the slots (min/max only when !is_min_max_deprecated && min/max_is_exact for every row group, rendered as SQL literals the FE parses with StatisticUtils.convertStatisticsToDouble :440-468; strings/binary/INT96/NaN omitted), get_file_schema (compute_node_service.rs:682-697) fills the field and logs files/rows/with_stats; build.rs:70-105 patch-presence check extended. FE: TableFunctionTable.getFileSchema (:688-731) builds an immutable FilesStatistics (exact from footers, or bytes/width estimate with exact=false) and logs one INFO line per statement; computeFileScanNode emits rows = sum(num_rows), per-column statistic by mode: `rows_ranges` (default) = UNKNOWN-typed statistic with finite min/max, real nullsFraction, ndv=1 (the estimator's own post-predicate state, honoured by StatisticRangeValues.from :52-54 and overlapPercentWith :90-107, so range predicates get overlap/length instead of 0.5 while join estimation stays on the conservative max(L,R) path of StatisticsCalculator.java:1222-1242); `rows_ranges_ndv` = ESTIMATE-typed with ndv=min(nonNullRows, max-min+1) for integral/date/decimal columns. visitOperator (:245-300) then applies the scan's own conjuncts; PlanNode.computeStatistics (:578-587) makes EXPLAIN COSTS show the new cardinalities. Part B: realCost = 0.5 cpu + 2 mem + 1.5 net (CostModel.java:129-135); BROADCAST exchange = 3.5*S (x1000 if S > exec_mem_limit, :426-429), single-node SHUFFLE has net=0 when enable_local_shuffle_agg (:437-440), broadcast probe penalty clamp(ln(rowsR/1e5),1,12) vs shuffle clamp(...,1,3) (HashJoinCostModel.java:141-156). For q05 at 1 CN with real stats (L=6e9x32 B, R=2.28e8x16 B): stock model SHUFFLE 3.95e11 vs BROADCAST 1.35e13 (34x, penalty) or 7.6e11 with exec_mem_limit raised (1.9x) -> lineitem still parked; with enable_local_shuffle_agg=false it is a coin flip (6.9e11 vs 7.6e11); with the GPU probe-penalty cap BROADCAST wins 3.1e11 vs 6.9e11, so lineitem stays in its scan fragment as the streamed probe (the standalone shape). q03 at 4 CN needs broadcast_row_limit >= 7.2e8 (guard) and the cap (2.5e11 vs 3.2e11) to broadcast the 2.33 GB orders x customer side instead of shuffling 58 GB of lineitem. Per-statement statistics mean no shared state, no cache invalidation, and cancellation semantics unchanged (existing future.get at TableFunctionTable.java:713).",

- ooc-sort-dev: Use when developing, building, testing, or iterating on the disk-backed (out-of-core) sort implementation for cudf-polars in ~/bzaitlen/test-data/ooc-sort/. Covers installing into the rapidsmpf container env, running streaming sort tests, and the phase-by-phase implementation workflow.
- build-errors: Use this skill when the build fails, compilation errors occur, or you see undefined references, linker errors, CUDA compilation issues, missing headers, or template instantiation failures. Analyzes errors, suggests fixes, and iteratively rebuilds until success.
- build-sirius-starrocks: Build the Sirius-as-StarRocks-CN stack on a fresh GPU box — UCX, nixl, libsirius, StarRocks FE, and the Rust CN. Use when standing the stack up from scratch, recovering a broken toolchain (g++/ld/nvml shims, CUDA 13, no-root conda deps), applying the StarRocks proto patch, or relocating pixi/cargo/Maven onto local NVMe.
- cn-tuning: Size Sirius StarRocks CN memory and operator budgets for a given GPU box and TPC-H scale factor. Use when choosing GPU_MEM, STAGING, HOST_MEM, hash_partition_bytes, scan_task_batch_size, or when a query OOMs / exhausts the exchange arena / looks like an engine bug that is actually mis-sizing. Covers the derived-flag path vs a full sirius.yaml.
- dataset-manager: Use this skill to generate benchmark datasets (TPC-H, TPC-DS, etc.). Trigger when the user needs test data at a specific scale factor for benchmarking or testing. Supports parquet and duckdb output formats.
- log-analyzer: Use this skill to analyze Sirius query execution logs — to find why a query is slow, diagnose validation errors (wrong results), spot excessive downgrading, identify pipeline gaps, or compare two runs of the same query. Trigger whenever the user mentions a Sirius log file, says "look at this log", asks about per-operator time, pipeline gaps, memory pressure, downgrade behavior, validation/correctness mismatches, or wants to compare two query runs. Also use as a hand-off target from race-check (for two-run comparisons), runtime-errors (for "where did the query stall before hang"), and validate (for diffing the bad run against a good run). This is the log-only counterpart to profile-analyzer (nsys) and optimization-advisor (source-level guidance).
- module-context: Automatically identify which dependency library modules are relevant to a task and load their API documentation into context. Use PROACTIVELY before implementing features, fixing bugs, or writing new operators — analyzes the task description and loads cudf, rmm, duckdb, cucascade module docs to improve code quality. Trigger when the user asks to implement, add, fix, or modify GPU operators, pipeline components, memory management, joins, aggregations, sorting, expressions, or data I/O.
- module-discover: Discover and document a dependency library or submodule — analyzes all uses within the codebase, divides the library into logical modules, identifies which modules are used, and generates LLM-consumable API documentation for each module. Use when the user wants to understand a library dependency, map its modules, or generate API reference docs for a submodule.
- optimization-advisor: Use this skill to find exactly which source code to optimize for better GPU performance. Maps nsys profile hotspots to specific Sirius source files and functions, classifies bottlenecks as GPU-bound, CPU-bound, or sync-bound, and recommends actionable code changes. Trigger when the user wants to know what to optimize, where to focus coding effort, or wants source-level optimization guidance. This skill focuses on actionable source code targets — for generating performance reports and measurements, use profile-analyzer instead.
- pr-digest: Generates a "learning" PR-review digest — a markdown file at PR_digests/PR_digest_<N>.md that explains what a GitHub PR does, why, and exactly where in the code, with clickable file/line links and trimmed diffs. Use this whenever the user shares a GitHub PR URL (e.g. github.com/owner/repo/pull/1234) and wants to understand, summarize, review, walk through, or get up to speed on what changed — phrases like "can you review this PR", "what does this PR do", "help me understand this pull request", "summarize the changes in PR
- pre-commit-cleanup: Clean the current Git changes before committing. Use when preparing to commit or when the pre-commit cleanliness hook blocks a commit.
- profile-analyzer: Use this skill to understand why a Sirius query is slow, identify GPU bottlenecks, or detect performance regressions. Generates reports with kernel occupancy, memory bandwidth, operator attribution, and cross-run comparisons. Trigger when the user mentions profiling, nsys, GPU utilization, kernel analysis, performance reports, or wants to compare query timings across runs. This skill focuses on measurement and reporting — for mapping hotspots to source code fixes, use optimization-advisor instead.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- tpch-2host: Bring up Sirius StarRocks CNs across two physical GB200 hosts with nixl over cross-host NVLink, and the matching stock StarRocks (engine B) two-machine baseline. Use when replicating the two-host experiment, setting SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_ARENA=fabric, debugging a 0.4 GB/s cuda_ipc fallback, or running engine B as 1 FE + 1 BE per host.
- tpch-bench: Operate the Sirius-as-StarRocks-CN demo and its TPC-H benchmark on the 4x GB200 box. Use when bringing the multi-GPU (N-CN, one CN per GPU) cluster up or down, running a query or the 22-query sweep, verifying the nixl/NVLink transport, triaging a failing/hanging/slow query, checking results against DuckDB, or reproducing the A-vs-B comparison against stock StarRocks.
- tpch-cn-sweep: Run the 22-query TPC-H sweep against a Sirius StarRocks CN cluster on any box, scale factor, data path, or GPU count. Use when launching bench.sh, sizing GPU_MEM/STAGING, checking results against the DuckDB oracle, or triaging pass/wedge/refused rows. Not the in-process Sirius-vs-DuckDB benchmark skill; not the GB200-hardcoded tpch-bench ops skill.
- update-docs: Use this skill to update Super Sirius documentation after code changes. # Plan: best solutions for the four SF1000 blockers, and the workflows that deliver them

Written 2026-09-03 15:20 UTC from the report `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md`
(sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/` (indexed by `WORKFLOW-PLAN.md` there).
Working tree for all code: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-*` worktrees of the sirius-stacks clone,
one branch per fix off `perf/profile-sf1000` (45dab3be = d24f02c4 + aggregate gate + async dispatch + Quent probes).
Never the shared clone `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius`. No pushes, no PRs until asked.

## The four issues

| # | issue | where it lives | measured cost today (SF1000, 1 CN, 100 GiB pool) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The OOM reschedule loop has no feasibility check | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp` (:263 reservation gate, :330-420 reschedule, MAX_RETRIES=100, 50 ms sleep) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 take 54-232 s to die (775 s of a 910 s sweep); 17,917 "0 bytes freed, proceeding with partial reservation" lines |
| 2 | No per-query parked-output bookkeeping | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs` (:291-316 process-wide wipe on Err), `compute_node_service.rs` (:449-476 cancel is result-store only), `local_exchange.rs` (removals only in take_ready) | 0-38 GB of a dead query's parked output survives into later queries; dead query's queued senders still run (q22 cold 4110 vs 943 ms) |
| 3 | The FE plans every FILES() scan at 1 row | StarRocks FE `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (:664-676), `TableFunctionTable.java` (file sizes at :611, schema RPC), `PGetFileSchemaResult` (proto :647-650), CN `file_schema.rs` | every distribution decision is data-blind: 1 CN broadcasts 3.79B lineitem rows into q04's semi join, 4 CNs shuffle 3.23B rows for q03; all six failures are one plan shape |
| 4 | Six queries cannot run on 1 CN | fragment cut (FE) + receiver-first full materialisation (`engine.rs` run_fragment_inner, `local_exchange.rs`) + parked repositories outside the downgrade sweep (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300`) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 OOM; standalone Sirius runs them in 2.7-6.5 s |

## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)

1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.

## Evaluation criteria (judges score 1-5 each)

1. Does it fix the measured failure at SF1000 on this box (which queries, predicted numbers, how verified)?
2. Correctness risk and blast radius (which paths change for the 15 passing queries; determinism; cancellation).
3. Size and reviewability as an upstream PR (target layer in the carve plan: engine `src/` -> dev PR; CN `experimental/starrocks` -> fork PR; FE -> checked-in patch), tests it needs.
4. Effort and dependencies (what must land first; FE rebuild; proto change).
5. Measurability: an acceptance test that a reviewer can rerun in minutes plus the SF1000 arm.

## Acceptance tests (must exist before implementation is "done")

| fix | unit / component test | SF1000 verification (orchestrator-run, one arm at a time) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Catch2 test in `test/cpp/pipeline/` driving a task through the reschedule path with a memory space that never frees: query fails within a bounded number of attempts with the new error text; contention case still retries | 1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21: time-to-fail <= 5 s each (was 54-232 s), error names parked bytes; the 15 passing queries unchanged (warm medians within noise, `compare.py` set unchanged) |
| 2 | Rust tests in `engine.rs`/`local_exchange.rs`/`compute_node_service.rs`: failure drops only that query's slots; queued senders of a failed query are skipped; cancel drops parked outputs; translation failure drops slots in hand | 1 CN sweep in the same order as before: `[gpu_pool] allocated` returns to baseline after each failure (was +4.7..+38 GB), q22 cold no longer inflated, no `fragment run started` for a dead query after its failure |
| 3 | FE unit test (Java) for the new statistics path; CN test if the proto changes; `EXPLAIN COSTS` golden outputs for q03 q04 q05 q22 at 1 and 4 CNs showing real cardinalities and the new join sides | 1 CN and 4 CN sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six: plan shapes recorded, timings vs the campaign table, oracle compares |
| 4 | Fusion: translator/CN tests that a single-destination local exchange fuses and the fused plan matches the sender+receiver plan; spill: Catch2 test that a parked repository is swept to HOST and relayed back | 1 CN: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass with oracle MATCH; report their times against standalone (2.7-6.5 s) |

## Workflows

**A. Design exploration (`fix/design-workflow.js`).** Per issue, three independent designers with different angles (surgical minimum, robust design, what upstream would accept), each reads the report finding, the evidence and the code and returns a design (mechanism, files, tests, risks, predicted effect). Two judges per issue score the three against the criteria and pick or merge. One synthesizer per issue writes the spec `scratchpad/fix/designs/<issue>-SPEC.md`. A final integrator checks the four specs for interactions (fail-fast vs bookkeeping ordering; fusion vs spill vs cardinalities) and writes the build order.

**B. Implementation (`fix/implement-workflow.js`).** Per issue in its own worktree: implementer (tests first, then code, build, run the unit tests; commits with Conventional Commits and the Claude trailer), adversarial reviewer, fixer, verifier (fresh build + tests + clippy/fmt/pre-commit). Agents never start clusters or use GPUs other than the one assigned to their worktree (fix 1: GPU 0, fix 2: GPU 1, fix 3: none, fix 4: GPU 2). The orchestrator then runs the SF1000 arms from the table above, one at a time, and an integration branch with all four for the final sweep.

**C. Report.** `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-top4-fixes-report.md`: per fix, what changed, tests, SF1000 before/after, what is left; plus the PR plan (branch, base, size) for when pushing is asked for.

## Status log
- 15:20 UTC: worktrees `fix-oom-failfast`, `fix-parked-bookkeeping`, `fix-files-cardinality`, `fix-fragment-fusion` being created and built; design workflow launched.

# SF1000 profiling: planning / cardinality / backpressure — evidence bundle and analysis plan

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +
9a5a4da6 (async sender dispatch) + 45dab3be (Quent probes: scan_split_read, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels).
Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)
- survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt, qNN.verbose.txt   FE EXPLAIN COSTS / VERBOSE for all 22 queries (fragments, join distribution, cardinality: 1 everywhere)
- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)
- standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt                   DuckDB/Sirius EXPLAIN of the same SQL (the stats-aware planner's choice)
- <arm>-cnlog.json (cnlog_extract.py), <arm>-quent.txt / .json (quent_bp.py), card-compare-<arm>.txt (card_compare.py), results.md (results_table.py)
- ../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv                  DuckDB CPU oracle answers; compare-*.txt

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## Facts added after the 1-CN sweep (13:19 UTC)
5. Supported on the CN path at SF1000 (1 CN, 100 GiB pool): q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 pass (15). Fail: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 = OOM at GPU_SCAN after 100 reschedules
   (101 s, 168 s, 232 s, 104 s, 54 s, 114 s to die; 2500-5600 reschedule warnings each, see cn1-cnlog.txt); q16 = translator gap ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does not model").
6. q15 returned 0 rows in run 1 and 1 row in runs 0 and 2 on 1 CN: streams 18 and 22 (the revenue = max(revenue) join output) carried 0 rows in run 1 while every other stream was identical.
   The build has the canonical float-sum sort gated OFF (SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS unset), so the two independently computed FP64 sums can differ in the last bits. Follow-up arms cn1-canon-q15 / cn1-nocanon-q15 test this.
7. Engine executor pools default to pipeline num_threads: 4 (docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94); Quent "Queued" time per fragment is the wait for one of those slots plus the memory reservation gate.
   1-CN q04: scan fragment 37 tasks, Queued sum 19.9 s vs Computing 4.7 s inside a 1.2 s wall; join fragment requested 253 GB of reservations for a 61 GB summed peak (4x over-estimate).
8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".
9. FE plans with 4 CNs alive are in survey/explain4/ (plan-summary-4cn.txt); diff against plan-summary.txt shows whether node count changes any distribution decision.
10. Plan-node enum decode for the dumps (TPlanNodeType(N)): survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt (4 HASH_JOIN, 6 AGGREGATION, 8 SORT, 9 EXCHANGE, 17 FILE_SCAN, 28 PROJECT, ...).
11. The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. The FE's fragment cut (what is broadcast/shuffled) is fixed before any of this.
12. The FE's plan DEPENDS on the number of alive CNs even with cardinality 1 everywhere: with 4 CNs most joins flip from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED (shuffle) and fragment counts rise (q02 13->16, q08 11->16, q09 9->12; q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q04/q12/q14/q19 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q15 -> BUCKET_SHUFFLE). survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) vs survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt (4 CNs); card-compare-cn4.txt uses the 4-CN plans (q03 exch2 = 3.23B lineitem rows shuffled, q12 exch1 = 1.5B orders rows shuffled).
13. 4-CN staging leases per query (cn4-quent.txt, attributed by time): q07.r1 747 leases / 141.5 GB moved / 92.9 s summed lease-held time inside a 1.79 s query, max 64 concurrent leases per CN; q04.r1 360 leases / 48.8 GB; q01.r1 14 leases / 0.06 GB. Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).
14. Standalone (one GPU, 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics) runs the same 15 queries; standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt holds its plans. 1-CN vs standalone warm medians (ms): q01 5073/4882, q02 1246/571, q03 3106/3050, q07 3476/3266, q11 970/336, q15 4685/2627, q20 4171/3023, q22 943/496 (results.md).
15. 12	## 0. Summary
13	
14	Replace the hard-coded `setOutputRowCount(1)` in `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (FE
15	`sql/optimizer/statistics/StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`) with
16	`rows = sum(file bytes) / sum(getTypeSize of the inferred schema)` for `TableFunctionTable` scans. Both inputs

23	(measured, section 2.3) and preserves the ordering that matters (lineitem > partsupp/orders > customer/part >
24	supplier > nation > region). It fixes C1 (`card_all_one=True` for all 22 plans) and the class of P3 decisions
25	where a tiny dimension is the shuffled or broadcast side. It does **not** by itself un-break the six 1-CN

33	## 1. The measured failure
34	
35	- **Measured.** `card_all_one=True` for all 22 plans (`survey/plan-summary.txt`); every `FileScanNode`,
36	  join and exchange prints `cardinality: 1` (`survey/explain/q05.costs.txt` lines 13, 27, ... 352). Actual

39	- **Measured source.** `StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`:

41	  ```java
42	  private Void computeFileScanNode(Operator node, ExpressionContext context,
43	                                   Map<ColumnRefOperator, Column> columnRefOperatorColumnMap) {
44	      // Use default statistics for now.
45	      Statistics.Builder builder = Statistics.builder();
46	      for (ColumnRefOperator columnRefOperator : columnRefOperatorColumnMap.keySet()) {

57	  external `FileTable` through `visitLogicalFileScan`/`visitPhysicalFileScan` (`:655-662`). The physical
58	  FILES() operator has no override (`sql/optimizer/operator/OperatorVisitor.java:454-456` falls through to
59	  `visitOperator`), so the row count of a FILES() group is set exactly once, from the logical operator.
60	- **Measured consequences** (report P1/P3/P5): with every child at 1 row, `Statistics.getOutputSize`
61	  (`sql/optimizer/statistics/Statistics.java:88-106`) is the sum of the projected type widths, so the
62	  BROADCAST/SHUFFLE choice is width arithmetic plus the CN count; `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit`

67	## 2. Mechanism
68	
69	### 2.1 What changes
70	
71	`FE/sql/optimizer/statistics/StatisticsCalculator.java`, function `computeFileScanNode` only:
72	
73	```java
74	private Void computeFileScanNode(Operator node, ExpressionContext context,
75	                                 Map<ColumnRefOperator, Column> columnRefOperatorColumnMap) {
76	    Statistics.Builder builder = Statistics.builder();
77	    for (ColumnRefOperator columnRefOperator : columnRefOperatorColumnMap.keySet()) {
78	        builder.addColumnStatistic(columnRefOperator, ColumnStatistic.unknown());
79	    }
80	    // Column statistics stay UNKNOWN (no min/max/NDV in the schema RPC). The row count is estimated
81	    // from the listed file bytes so that join sides and exchange types are no longer decided at 1 row.
82	    double rowCount = estimateFilesRowCount(node);
83	    builder.setOutputRowCount(rowCount);
84	    builder.setTableRowCountMayInaccurate(rowCount != 1);
85	    context.setStatistics(builder.build());
86	    return visitOperator(node, context);
87	}
88	
89	// bytes / typed row width. Only for FILES() (TableFunctionTable); the external FILE table keeps 1.
90	private static double estimateFilesRowCount(Operator node) {
91	    if (!Config.files_query_estimate_row_count) {
92	        return 1;
93	    }
94	    Table table = node instanceof LogicalScanOperator ? ((LogicalScanOperator) node).getTable()
95	            : node instanceof PhysicalScanOperator ? ((PhysicalScanOperator) node).getTable() : null;
96	    if (!(table instanceof TableFunctionTable)) {
97	        return 1;
98	    }
99	    TableFunctionTable files = (TableFunctionTable) table;
100	    if (files.isListFilesOnly()) {                   // list_files_only: one row per listed entry is a different scan
101	        return 1;
102	    }
103	    long bytes = 0;
104	    for (TBrokerFileStatus f : files.loadFileList()) {
105	        if (!f.isDir) {
106	            bytes += Math.max(0, f.size);
107	        }
108	    }
109	    long width = 0;
110	    for (Column c : files.getFullSchema()) {
111	        width += Math.max(1, c.getType().getTypeSize());
112	    }
113	    if (bytes <= 0 || width <= 0) {
114	        return 1;
115	    }
116	    return Math.max(1, (double) bytes / width);
117	}
118	```

200	## 3. Behaviour under the FE cost model (inference; the acceptance survey in section 5 is what settles it)
201	
202	### 3.1 The cost function as it applies to this deployment (measured in source)
203	
204	- `CostModel.getRealCost` (`sql/optimizer/cost/CostModel.java:129-135`): `0.5*cpu + 2*mem + 1.5*net`.
205	- BROADCAST exchange (`CostModel.java:419-431`): `cpu = size*aliveBackendNumber`, `mem = size*beNum`,
206	  `net = max(size*beNum, 1)`, `beNum = max(1, aliveBackendNumber)`; multiplied by
207	  `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY = 1000` (`StatisticsEstimateCoefficient.java:60`) when
208	  `size > exec_mem_limit` (2 GiB, `qe/SessionVariable.java:1305-1307`). The Sirius CNs are COMPUTE NODEs, so
209	  `ConnectContext.getAliveBackendNumber()` (`qe/ConnectContext.java:1497-1503`) is 0 and a broadcast costs
210	  `3.5 * S_B` regardless of CN count (report P3, confirmed here).
211	- SHUFFLE exchange (`CostModel.java:432-441`): `cpu = size`, `net = size`, or `net = 0` when the FE has exactly
212	  one registered node (`system/SystemInfoService.java:246-248 isSingleBackendAndComputeNode`, counts registered
213	  not alive) and `enable_local_shuffle_agg` (default true, `SessionVariable.java:1229`) -> `2.0 * S` per side,
214	  or `0.5 * S`.
215	- Hash join (`sql/optimizer/cost/HashJoinCostModel.java`): cpu `:86-111` = build + probe + output;
216	  BROADCAST build `S_B`, probe `S_L * P_b`; SHUFFLE build `S_B / pf`, probe `S_L * P_s`. `getAvgProbeCost`
217	  `:134-156`: `P_b = clamp(ln(R_B / 1e5), 1, 12)` (`BOTTOM_NUMBER :58`, `BROADCAST_MAT_RATIO :62`),
218	  `P_s = clamp(ln(R_B / 1e5) - log2(2*pf), 1, 3)` (`SHUFFLE_MAX_RATIO :60`),
219	  `pf = max(aliveBE + aliveCN, dop)`. mem `:115-129`: BROADCAST `S_B * (aliveBE + aliveCN)`, SHUFFLE `S_B`.
220	- `dop` = `pipeline_dop` if set, else `max(1, avgCores/2)` (`SessionVariable.java:3964-3976`,
221	  `system/BackendResourceStat.java:210-213`); the CN heartbeats `available_parallelism()` as its core count
222	  (`experimental/starrocks/src/lib.rs:410, :519`). On this box that is tens of cores, so `pf` is 36-72 and
223	  `log2(2*pf)` is 6-7; the conclusions below hold for any `pf >= 4`.
224	- Broadcast guard (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-329`): reject broadcast iff
225	  `S_L < S_B * max(1, aliveBackendNumber) * 10 && R_B > 15,000,000` (`SessionVariable.java:1833-1836`).
226	
227	Sanity check against today's plans: with every side at 1 row, `P_b = P_s = 1`, and broadcast beats shuffle iff
228	`3.5*S_B < 2*(S_L + S_B)` at 1 CN (i.e. build width below ~1.3x probe width) and iff
229	`3.5*S_B + 2*4*S_B < 2*(S_L+S_B) + 2*S_B` at 4 CNs (build width below ~0.27x probe width). That reproduces
230	every observed 1-CN/4-CN flip in `plan-summary.txt` vs `plan-summary-4cn.txt` (q03 build 16 B vs probe 24 B:
231	BROADCAST at 1 CN, PARTITIONED at 4; customer 4 B vs orders 20 B: BROADCAST at both), so the model used below is
232	the one the FE actually ran.
233	
234	### 3.2 With row counts: the probe-cache term decides, not the exchange bytes
235	
236	For a build of `R_B` estimated rows the broadcast probe carries `S_L * (P_b - P_s) * 0.5` of extra cost
237	against the shuffle's `2*S_L` (or `0.5*S_L`) exchange. `P_b - P_s` reaches `log2(2*pf)` (about 6) as soon as
238	`R_B >= 1e5 * e^(1 + log2(2pf))`, i.e. a few million rows. Consequences:
239	
240	- builds below ~3e5 rows: `P_b = P_s = 1`, broadcast wins as today (nation, region, filtered supplier,
241	  the 1-row region of q02, the single GERMANY nation of q11);
242	- builds between ~3e5 and ~1e7 rows: close call, depends on `pf` and on whether the FE counts network cost;
243	- builds above ~1e7 rows: shuffle wins at 1 CN and at 4 CNs, independent of the ×1000 memory penalty (which
244	  only starts at 2 GiB, i.e. >= ~1e8 rows of a narrow build).
245	
246	Worked example, q05 exch 9 (the failing fragment of P1), 1 CN, network counted, `pf = 36`:
247	
248	| term | BROADCAST orders_f x customer (build) | SHUFFLE both |
249	|---|---:|---:|
250	| build `R_B`, `S_B` | 1.42e8 rows (5.69e8 x 0.5 x 0.5, then `max` with customer 1.12e8), 12 B -> 1.70e9 B | same |
251	| probe `S_L` (lineitem, 28 B projected) | 1.23e9 x 28 = 34.5e9 B | same |
252	| exchange | 3.5 x 1.70e9 = 5.9e9 | 2.0 x (34.5e9 + 1.70e9) = 72.4e9 |
253	| join cpu x 0.5 | 0.5 x (1.70e9 + 34.5e9 x 7.26) = 126.1e9 (`P_b = ln(1420)`) | 0.5 x (1.70e9/36 + 34.5e9 x 1.09) = 18.8e9 |
254	| join mem x 2 | 3.4e9 | 3.4e9 |
255	| total | 135.4e9 | 94.6e9 (40.3e9 with network ignored) |
256	
257	Shuffle wins by 1.4x-3.4x, so lineitem still leaves its scan fragment through a `HASH_PARTITIONED` sink and is
258	parked in full; the six 1-CN failures are unchanged by this fix (agrees with the report's P1 caveat, for a
259	different reason than the memory penalty it named). Raising `exec_mem_limit` does not help: the probe term
260	dominates before the penalty is reached, so this design does not ask for it.

286	## 4. Blast radius
287	
288	Paths that change: only FILES() scans (`LogicalTableFunctionTableScanOperator`, whose constructor asserts
289	`table instanceof TableFunctionTable`, `sql/optimizer/operator/logical/LogicalTableFunctionTableScanOperator.java:44`).
290	Unchanged by construction: external `FileTable` scans (same function, `instanceof` guard fails -> 1),
291	`list_files_only` FILES() (`isListFilesOnly`, `TableFunctionTable.java:432`), OLAP/Iceberg/Hive/Delta/Paimon
292	statistics, every other estimator branch. `INSERT ... FROM FILES()` (load type) gets the same estimate for its
293	scan; its plan is scan -> sink and has no join to re-decide.
294	
295	Second-order FE effects that need a companion setting or a landing order, all triggered by real row counts:
296	
297	1. **CTE reuse.** The bench queries declare all eight tables as `WITH t AS (SELECT * FROM FILES(...))` and
298	   q15/q17/q18/q21/q11/q02 consume one of them 2-3 times. Reuse vs inline is costed in the memo
299	   (`CostModel.java:558-577`, ratio `cbo_cte_reuse_rate` 1.15, `SessionVariable.java:1511`); with 1-row
300	   statistics inline always won. With real statistics the CBO may materialise a FILES() CTE once through a
301	   `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK`, which the CN refuses by name (`compute_node_service.rs:1519`, test
302	   `:3568-3588`). Companion: `SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse = false` (`SessionVariable.java:1505-1506`;
303	   `CTEContext.needInline:157-190` returns true when `!enableCTE`). Cheap, reversible, and it is the behaviour
304	   the CN supports today.
305	2. **Semi/anti commutation.** `JoinCommutativityRule` (`rule/transformation/JoinCommutativityRule.java:34-44`)
306	   maps LEFT_SEMI <-> RIGHT_SEMI; the translator accepts LEFT_SEMI, LEFT_ANTI, RIGHT_ANTI,
307	   NULL_AWARE_LEFT_ANTI but not RIGHT_SEMI (`node_translator.rs:1743-1762`). Land the one-arm translator
308	   change (report item 5, `TJoinOp::RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN => (JoinType::RightSemi, JoinOutput::Right)`) first, or
309	   accept that q04/q20/q21 may be refused in the SF1000 arm and record it.
310	3. **Aggregation stages.** One-stage aggregation stays disabled because the column statistics are still
311	   unknown (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:411-415`); two-phase plans are unchanged.
312	4. **Runtime filters.** FE build-size thresholds see larger builds and may attach fewer RFs; the CN drops
313	   them anyway (report P2, `grep runtime_filter` over the translator finds only a fixture).
314	
315	Operational: the FE must be rebuilt and redeployed (`pixi run fe-build`, then the packaged FE under
316	`starrocks/output/fe`); the CN binary, proto, translator and engine are untouched, so fixes 1, 2 and 4 can be
317	built and tested independently of this one. CI (`.github/workflows/experimental.yml:50-58`) applies only
318	`nixl-exchange-proto.patch` by name for the CN build; an FE-only patch needs no CI change.

413	## 8. Risks, ranked
414	
415	1. **1-CN plan regressions (q03, q12; possibly q07, q10)**, inference from section 3.2. Mitigations: the
416	   mutable knob (turn off on a 1-CN deployment without a rebuild); run fix 2 first so B4 leaks do not stack on
417	   the newly parked bytes; the follow-up that actually fixes this is a second, separate FE patch neutralising
418	   the CPU-cache probe penalty for this deployment (`HashJoinCostModel.getAvgProbeCost:134-156`, return 1.0
419	   under a config), which is out of scope here and belongs to the robust design.
420	2. **Translator refusals for RIGHT_SEMI** (q04, q20, q21), inference from `JoinCommutativityRule` becoming
421	   cost-relevant. Mitigation: land the translator arm first (report item 5, small), or measure and record.
422	3. **CTE reuse -> MULTI_CAST refused** (q15, q17, q18, q21, q11, q02), inference. Mitigation:
423	   `cbo_cte_reuse=false` in the harness; also protects the demo queries.
424	4. **Estimator bias** (0.2x-6x). Decisions in the studied set hinge on >= 10x ratios or on thresholds far
425	   from the estimates (q12 build 3.85e7 vs 1.5e7 limit); a table with many string columns and a single-row
426	   dimension is the failure mode to watch (the dimension is over-estimated, the fact under-estimated, both
427	   still separated by orders of magnitude).
428	5. **Determinism/correctness**: none; the change is planning-only and the CN executes whatever fragment shape
429	   it receives (oracle compares in 6.3 confirm). Cancellation paths untouched.
430	6. **FE rebuild cost** for every iteration on the estimator; the knob keeps iterations on the plan side to
431	   config flips.

1	# Fix 3, robust design: real FILES() statistics in the StarRocks FE
2	
3	Angle: what a senior engineer ships for the long run. Written 2026-09-03 from the report
4	`starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md` (C1, P1, P3, P4, section 4),
5	the evidence bundle `scratchpad/perf/sf1000/`, and the source worktree
6	`/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` (FE = `experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks`).
7	Every number is **measured** (named evidence file) or marked **inference**. Code excerpts relied on are in the appendix.
8	
9	## 0. Summary
10	
11	Today the FE plans every `FILES()` scan at 1 row (`StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`), so every distribution
12	decision is arithmetic on column widths and node count (P3). This design has three parts:
13	
14	- **Part A, statistics (the fix).** The CN already opens every parquet footer for the schema RPC
15	  (`file_schema.rs:14-27`, 60 footers for lineitem). Extend `PGetFileSchemaResult` with per-file
16	  `num_rows`, `file_size` and per-column `null_count`/`min`/`max` (proto patch + CN + FE). The FE stores them on
17	  the per-statement `TableFunctionTable` and `computeFileScanNode` emits the exact row count plus finite column
18	  ranges. Fallback when the CN sends nothing: rows = bytes / row width from `TBrokerFileStatus.size`
19	  (`TableFunctionTable.java:611`), flagged `tableRowCountMayInaccurate`. Column NDV is a separate, flag-gated mode.
20	- **Part B, GPU-aware cost inputs (required for the six 1-CN failures).** Hand-computation of the FE cost code
21	  (section 4) shows that with real statistics the stock model *still* shuffles lineitem at 1 CN: the single-node
22	  shuffle has zero network cost (`CostModel.java:437-440`), a broadcast whose build exceeds `exec_mem_limit`
23	  (2 GiB) is multiplied by 1000 (`CostModel.java:426-429`), and the broadcast probe carries a CPU-cache penalty
24	  of up to 12x vs 3x for shuffle (`HashJoinCostModel.java:141-156`). Three existing session variables
25	  (`exec_mem_limit`, `enable_local_shuffle_agg`, `broadcast_row_limit`) plus one flag-gated 4-line cost change
26	  (`enable_sirius_gpu_join_cost`: cap the broadcast probe penalty at the shuffle cap) make the FE choose
27	  "broadcast the small side, stream lineitem", which is the standalone plan that passes all six.
28	- **Part C, rollout.** Mutable FE config `files_query_statistics_mode = off | rows | rows_ranges | rows_ranges_ndv`
29	  (kill switch without restart), `SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse = false` until the CN implements
30	  `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK`, and translator `RIGHT_SEMI` (plan item 5) **before** enabling in the sweep,
31	  because real statistics make the FE commute LEFT SEMI joins (q04/q18/q20/q21) into a join type the translator
32	  refuses today.
33	
34	Predicted (inference, section 7): q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 pass on 1 CN at roughly standalone time (2.8-5.4 s + ~0.2 s
35	head); q21 additionally needs item 5. At 4 CNs q03 moves ~7 GB instead of 58 GB, q12 ~1.5 GB instead of 23 GB,
36	q22 stops broadcasting 1.5B orders rows; q04 stops parking 30.8 GB of lineitem keys. Effort ~4 engineer-days plus
37	one multi-hour FE rebuild.
38	
39	## 1. The problem, measured
40	
41	- `card_all_one=True` for all 22 plans (survey/plan-summary.txt); actuals up to 6.0e9 rows per exchange
42	  (card-compare-cn1.txt, card-compare-cn4.txt). Root cause `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode`
43	  (`StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`): `builder.setOutputRowCount(1)`, every column `ColumnStatistic.unknown()`.
44	- Consequences confirmed in source (C1): `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` inert (needs right rows > 15M,
45	  `EnforceAndCostTask.java:324-325`), CTE inlining always wins, `JoinCommutativityRule` never commutes semi/anti,
46	  the fragment cut is decided by widths and node count (P3 mechanism, `HashJoinCostModel.java:115-127`).
47	- All six 1-CN failures are one shape: unfiltered lineitem leaf -> `HASH_PARTITIONED` sink -> parked in full
48	  (P1 table: 171-245 GB projections vs a 107 GB pool). Standalone Sirius with DuckDB's parquet statistics streams
49	  lineitem as the probe of a hash join built on the filtered dimension chain and passes all six
50	  (standalone-failed/runs/q05.explain.txt:50-61, `~6,110,827,680 rows` probe vs `~61,617,442 rows` build).
51	- Row counts already exist in two places: `TBrokerFileStatus.size` per file on the FE
52	  (`TableFunctionTable.java:606-613`) and the parquet footer the CN already parses
53	  (`file_schema.rs:19-27`, `ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::metadata()`; `FileMetaData::num_rows`,
54	  `ColumnChunkMetaData::statistics()` in parquet-rs 59.2.0 `file/metadata/mod.rs:548,1072`).
55	- The schema RPC is per statement and per FILES() reference with no cache (P4: 8 RPCs per query, 73-114 ms);
56	  the lineitem call is busy 28 ms (cn1/cluster.log:923). Reading statistics off the same footers adds no I/O.
57	
58	## 2. Design overview
59	
60	```
61	FE analyzer                      CN (Rust)                         FE optimizer
62	QueryAnalyzer:2192 ---> get_file_schema RPC ----> file_schema.rs      StatisticsCalculator
63	 new TableFunctionTable           parquet footers (already read)      .computeFileScanNode
64	   .getFileSchema():688   <---- PGetFileSchemaResult                    rows = sum(num_rows)
65	   parses schema + NEW              schema[]                             ranges = min/max per column
66	   file_statistics[]      NEW:      file_statistics[] {path,num_rows,    nulls  = null_count/rows
67	   -> FilesStatistics                file_size, columns[]{col_name,      NDV    = mode-dependent
68	      (immutable, per stmt)          null_count,min,max,uncompressed}}  -> Statistics (exact) or
69	                                                                         bytes/width fallback (inaccurate)
70	```
71	
72	Then the CBO does what it does for OLAP tables: real `getOutputSize`, real range selectivities, armed broadcast
73	guard, join commutation, CTE cost. Part B keeps its cost constants from steering a GPU cluster with CPU heuristics.
74	
75	## 3. Mechanism
76	
77	### 3.1 Wire: `gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto` (patched, Sirius-only)
78	
79	```proto
80	// Sirius extension: per-file statistics read from parquet footers by the compute node.
81	message PFileColumnStatistics {
82	    optional string col_name = 1;
83	    optional int64  null_count = 2;         // summed over row groups; absent if any row group lacks it
84	    optional string min = 3;                // SQL literal per logical type (ints/decimals as decimal text,
85	    optional string max = 4;                //   DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD', DATETIME 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]');
86	                                            //   absent for strings/binary, INT96, NaN, deprecated/inexact stats
87	    optional int64  uncompressed_bytes = 5; // for average row size
88	    optional int64  distinct_count = 6;     // only when the writer recorded it (rare); FE ignores in phase A
89	}
90	message PFileStatistics {
91	    optional string path = 1;
92	    optional int64  num_rows = 2;
93	    optional int64  file_size = 3;
94	    repeated PFileColumnStatistics columns = 4;
95	}
96	message PGetFileSchemaResult {
97	    required StatusPB status = 1;
98	    repeated PSlotDescriptor schema = 2;
99	    repeated PFileStatistics file_statistics = 3;   // Sirius extension; absent from stock BEs
100	};
101	```
102	
103	Why per file, not totals: the FE merge is 20 lines, the payload is 60 files x 16 columns, and per-file rows are
104	what a later per-split pruning or a partial-footer failure needs. All fields optional: an old FE ignores field 3,
105	an old CN (or a stock BE) leaves it empty and the FE falls back (3.3).
106	
107	The patch lives beside the two existing ones (`experimental/starrocks/patches/*.patch`,
108	`scripts/apply-starrocks-patches.sh` applies them in glob order and treats "already applied" as success). The
109	new hunk at `internal_service.proto:647-650` does not overlap the nixl patch's hunk at `:786`, so the two apply
110	independently. FE Java classes are regenerated from the proto at build time
111	(`fe/fe-core/pom.xml:1136-1149`, jprotobuf `--java_out`), so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`).
112	The CN regenerates via prost in `build.rs:26-56`; extend `require_exchange_proto_patch` (`build.rs:70-105`) to
113	also check for `message PFileStatistics`, so a stale submodule fails with the remedy instead of a type error.

115	### 3.2 CN: `experimental/starrocks/src/file_schema.rs`, `compute_node_service.rs`
116	
117	- `parquet_file_schema(path)` (`file_schema.rs:14-50`) already has the footer in hand. Return a
118	  `FileFooter { slots: Vec<PSlotDescriptor>, stats: PFileStatistics }`. Row count: `metadata.file_metadata().num_rows()`.
119	  Per column (top-level primitive fields only, same iteration as today): sum `ColumnChunkMetaData::num_values`
120	  and `statistics().null_count_opt()` over row groups; min/max: take `min_bytes_opt/max_bytes_opt` only when
121	  `!is_min_max_deprecated() && min_is_exact() && max_is_exact()` for every row group, decode by the column's
122	  physical+logical type (INT32/INT64 with DATE/DECIMAL/plain annotations, DOUBLE/FLOAT excluding NaN,
123	  INT64 TIMESTAMP) and render as the SQL literal the FE parses with `StatisticUtils.convertStatisticsToDouble`
124	  (`statistic/StatisticUtils.java:440-468`: DATE/DATETIME via the FE date parsers, everything else `Double.parseDouble`).
125	  Strings/binary/INT96 get no min/max (the FE treats string ranges as infinite anyway,
126	  `StatisticRangeValues.java:77-88`). `uncompressed_bytes` = sum of `uncompressed_size`.
127	- `parquet_files_schema(paths)` (`file_schema.rs:62-99`) keeps the fail-closed schema-agreement contract and

129	- `compute_node_service.rs::get_file_schema` (`:682-697`) fills `file_statistics`; `file_schema_from_attachment`
130	  (`:1680-1707`) passes the paths through unchanged. The `#[instrument]` span gains `files`, `rows`, `with_stats`
131	  fields and one `info!` line per request so cn logs show what the FE was told.
132	- Optional, same function, P4 synergy: a bounded-concurrency footer read (`buffer_unordered(8)`) and a
133	  process-wide memo `(path, len, mtime) -> Arc<FileFooter>`; entries are immutable, the key changes when the file
134	  does, so no invalidation logic. Not required for correctness; ship separately if the reviewer prefers.

136	### 3.3 FE: statistics into the optimizer
137	
138	`TableFunctionTable` (`catalog/TableFunctionTable.java`):
139	
140	- `getFileSchema()` (`:688-731`) already receives the result; after the `schema` loop, build
141	  `FilesStatistics.fromRpc(result.file_statistics, columns, fileStatuses)` and store it in a new final field.
142	  If `file_statistics` is empty, `FilesStatistics.estimateFromBytes(fileStatuses, columns)`:
143	  rows = sum(size) / sum(type width of the inferred columns), `exact=false`.
144	  One `LOG.info` per statement: path, files, rows, bytes, source (`footer|estimated`), columns with ranges,
145	  RPC ms (3.6).
146	- New immutable holder `catalog/FilesStatistics.java`: `totalRows`, `totalBytes`, `exact`, per-column
147	  `{nullCount, min, max (as double via convertStatisticsToDouble, merged min/max across files), avgSize}`; a
148	  `columnStatistic(Column, Type, Mode)` factory.
149	
150	`StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (`:664-676`), reached from `visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan` (`:374-376`),
151	`visitLogicalFileScan`/`visitPhysicalFileScan` (`:655-662`):
152	
153	```java
154	Table table = (node instanceof LogicalScanOperator) ? ((LogicalScanOperator) node).getTable()
155	                                                     : ((PhysicalScanOperator) node).getTable();
156	FilesStatistics fs = (table instanceof TableFunctionTable && mode != OFF)
157	        ? ((TableFunctionTable) table).getFilesStatistics() : null;
158	Statistics.Builder builder = Statistics.builder();
159	for (ColumnRefOperator ref : colRefToColumnMetaMap.keySet()) {
160	    builder.addColumnStatistic(ref, fs == null ? ColumnStatistic.unknown()
161	                                               : fs.columnStatistic(colRefToColumnMetaMap.get(ref), ref.getType(), mode));
162	}
163	builder.setOutputRowCount(fs == null ? 1 : fs.getTotalRows());
164	builder.setTableRowCountMayInaccurate(fs != null && !fs.isExact());
165	context.setStatistics(builder.build());
166	return visitOperator(node, context);   // applies the scan's own conjuncts and limit, :245-300
167	```
168	
169	Every required column must get an entry (`Statistics.getColumnStatistic` throws on a missing one, `Statistics.java:118-125`).
170	`FileTable` scans (not `TableFunctionTable`) keep today's behaviour. Add `visitPhysicalTableFunctionTableScan`
171	symmetric to `:374` so physical re-derivation cannot fall back to the default.
172	
173	Column statistic per mode (`FilesStatistics.columnStatistic`):
174	
175	| mode | row count | column statistic | join-key estimate path |
176	|---|---|---|---|
177	| `off` | 1 | `unknown()` | today |
178	| `rows` | exact / estimated | `unknown()` | `max(L,R)` (`StatisticsCalculator.java:1222-1242`) |
179	| `rows_ranges` (default) | exact / estimated | type **UNKNOWN**, finite `min/max`, real `nullsFraction`, `averageRowSize` = type width (or `uncompressed/rows`), `distinctValuesCount = 1` | `max(L,R)`; range predicates use `overlap/length` (`StatisticRangeValues.java:102-107`) instead of 0.5 |
180	| `rows_ranges_ndv` | exact / estimated | type **ESTIMATE** for integral/date/decimal columns with `ndv = min(nonNullRows, max-min+1)`; strings/floats stay as in `rows_ranges` | `L*R/max(ndv)` (`estimateInnerJoinStatistics`, `:1711-1719`) |
181	
182	Why an UNKNOWN-typed statistic with a finite range is native, not a hack: the estimator itself produces that
183	state today (`estimatePredicateRange` rebuilds the column with the intersect range and `setType(columnStatistic.getType())`,
184	`BinaryPredicateStatisticCalculator.java:201-225`; the printed `o_orderdate-->[7.414848E8, 7.494336E8, ...] UNKNOWN`
185	in survey/explain/q04.costs.txt:102 is exactly it). `StatisticRangeValues.from` reads min/max/ndv regardless of type
186	(`:52-54`); `distinctValues == 1` is the marker the point-predicate branch uses for "unknown" (`:90-96`), so
187	equality selectivity stays 0.5 (no regression) while ranges become real. No FE code compares against the
188	`ColumnStatistic.unknown()` singleton by identity (grep, none). The `rows_ranges_ndv` heuristic is right for
189	dense surrogate keys (TPC-H `*_key`, nationkey, dates, quantities) and degrades to `ndv = rows` for sparse keys
190	(the usual PK-FK assumption); it is a mode, not the default, and the EXPLAIN gate picks between the two (6.2).
191	
192	### 3.4 FE cost inputs for a GPU cluster (Part B)
193	
194	Measured cost code (appendix A.4-A.6): `realCost = 0.5 cpu + 2 mem + 1.5 net` (`CostModel.java:129-135`).
195	Exchange BROADCAST: `cpu = S * aliveBackends` (0 here: the Sirius CNs register as COMPUTE NODEs, P3),
196	`mem = S`, `net = S`, all x1000 when `S > exec_mem_limit` (`:419-429`, default 2 GiB `SessionVariable.java:1305`).
197	Exchange SHUFFLE: `cpu = S*f`, `net = 0` when `enable_local_shuffle_agg && pipeline && single node` else `S*f`
198	(`:432-441`, `SystemInfoService.java:246-248`). Hash join: BROADCAST `cpu = R + L*pB, mem = R*N`;
199	SHUFFLE `cpu = R/p + L*pS, mem = R` with `pB = clamp(ln(rowsR/1e5), 1, 12)`, `pS = clamp(ln(rowsR/1e5) - log2(2p), 1, 3)`
200	(`HashJoinCostModel.java:87-156`, `BOTTOM_NUMBER = 100000` `:58`). Guard: broadcast rejected when
201	`L_bytes < R_bytes * 10 && rowsR > broadcast_row_limit(15M)` (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-327`).
202	
203	Three of the four levers are existing session variables; set once per cluster (`SET GLOBAL`, as the bench kit already
204	does for `enable_pipeline_engine`, `run-abc.sh:799`), shipped as `experimental/starrocks/conf/sirius-cbo-defaults.sql`
205	and applied by the launchers after the FE is up:
206	
207	| setting | value | why (source) |
208	|---|---|---|
209	| `exec_mem_limit` | 64 GiB (below the GPU pool; the CN does not enforce `TQueryOptions.mem_limit`: no `mem_limit` in `experimental/starrocks/src`) | removes the x1000 penalty on multi-GB broadcast builds (`CostModel.java:426-429`); builds of 1-10 GB are normal on a 100 GiB GPU pool |
210	| `enable_local_shuffle_agg` | `false` | on a Sirius CN a single-node shuffle parks the whole stream (B1); its network cost must be the bytes, not 0 (`CostModel.java:437-440`) |
211	| `broadcast_row_limit` | 2,000,000,000 | the guard protects CPU BE memory; without it q03's 7.2e8-row (est.) build is rejected although it is 2.3 GB real (section 4, case B) |
212	| `cbo_cte_reuse` | `false` | real costs can make CTE reuse win, which emits `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK`; the CN refuses it (`compute_node_service.rs:1519`, P5); revisit when plan item 9 lands |
213	| `enable_sirius_gpu_join_cost` (new, patch) | `true` | see below |
214	
215	The one code change (patch, `HashJoinCostModel.getAvgProbeCost`, `:141-156`): when the new session variable is set,
216	cap the BROADCAST cache penalty at `SHUFFLE_MAX_RATIO` (3) like the shuffle branch. The 12x-vs-3x split models
217	CPU cache misses of a large hash table; a GPU hash join keeps both builds in HBM. Four lines plus the variable.
218	Everything else in the model (bytes moved, memory per node, N-way replication) stays as upstream wrote it.
219	
220	### 3.5 Concurrency and cancellation
221	
222	- FE: statistics live on the per-statement `TableFunctionTable` created in
223	  `QueryAnalyzer.resolveTableFunctionTable` (`:2192-2196`); no shared mutable state, no cache, no invalidation.
224	  `Config` is read once per `computeFileScanNode`; a mode flip mid-statement cannot mix modes inside one plan
225	  because the mode is captured in `FilesStatistics` at RPC time.
226	- FE cancellation: the RPC wait is the existing `future.get()` (`TableFunctionTable.java:713`); an interrupt is
227	  already converted to `DdlException` (`:714-716`). Statistics add no new blocking. Pre-existing gap worth a
228	  separate line item: the wait is unbounded; a bounded `future.get(timeout)` is a one-line hardening.
229	- CN: the handler is async per request (`compute_node_service.rs:682-697`); statistics are a pure function of
230	  metadata already loaded; a cancelled FE statement simply discards the reply. The optional memo (3.2) stores
231	  immutable `Arc` entries keyed by `(path, len, mtime)`, so concurrent requests never observe a partial entry.
232	- Wire compatibility: all new fields optional; mixed FE/CN versions degrade to the bytes/width estimate, never
233	  to a failure.

415	## 8. Risks and failure modes
416	
417	Enumerated with the behaviour and the mitigation:
418	
419	1. **New plan shapes the CN cannot execute.** `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN` (translator `node_translator.rs:1743-1762`) for
420	   q04/q18/q20/q21; `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK` if CTE reuse wins (`compute_node_service.rs:1519`). Both fail
421	   closed with a named error (as q16 does today), no wrong result. Mitigation: item 5 lands first;
422	   `cbo_cte_reuse=false` in the defaults; `files_query_statistics_mode=off` kill switch. The EXPLAIN gate
423	   (6.2) catches both before any GPU run.
424	2. **Under-estimated build broadcast to every CN.** A wrong small-side estimate parks a large build on N GPUs.
425	   Bounded by `exec_mem_limit` (x1000 above 64 GiB est.) and, at run time, by fix 1 (fail fast) instead of
426	   54-232 s storms. The `max(L,R)` join rule of `rows_ranges` errs toward over-estimating intermediates
427	   (never under), which is the safe direction for this failure; `rows_ranges_ndv` can under-estimate joins on
428	   sparse keys, which is why it is a mode.
429	3. **q10-type over-estimation** (`max(L,R)` says 3e9 for lineitem ⋈ orders, real 1.15e8) makes the FE move
430	   the wide customer projection instead. Decided at the gate; the engine's in-fragment re-plan (C2) still
431	   applies inside the receiver.
432	4. **CN returns no statistics** (stock BE, non-parquet, remote URI): bytes/width estimate with
433	   `tableRowCountMayInaccurate=true`, log `source=estimated`. Plans as good as byte totals allow; the flag
434	   disables skew rewrites and one-stage aggregation (`DataSkew.java:161,194`, `EnforceAndCostTask.java:413`).
435	5. **Unreliable footer statistics** (deprecated/inexact min/max, writer bugs): min/max omitted per column ->
436	   infinite range = today's 0.5 behaviour; row counts are always exact in parquet. Statistics never affect
437	   correctness, only the plan.
438	6. **Partial footer failure**: the schema RPC already fails closed on any unreadable file (`file_schema.rs:62-99`);
439	   no partial-statistics state exists.
440	7. **Files change between analysis and execution**: statistics stale by one statement; harmless.
441	8. **Version skew FE/CN**: optional protobuf fields; either direction degrades to (4).
442	9. **Very large file counts**: footer reads already dominate the RPC (P4); the optional memo/concurrency (3.2)
443	   is the fix; statistics add no I/O.

445	    (`PushDownAggregateCollector.java:647`) -> pre-aggregation may be pushed below more joins (the q20 pattern,
446	    P5 SAJ-1). Visible at the gate; if it hurts, `cbo_push_down_aggregate_mode` is the lever.
447	11. **Determinism**: the plan depends on file statistics, which are deterministic per dataset; the
448	    `Collections.shuffle(nodeIds)` choice of which CN answers the RPC (`TableFunctionTable.java:706`) does not
449	    matter because every CN reads the same footers.
450	12. **Upstream drift**: the patch touches five FE files; `computeFileScanNode` and `getFileSchema` are stable
451	    since 3.x. Keep the hunks small and re-apply on submodule bumps as with the nixl patch.

1	# Design: real FILES() cardinalities in the StarRocks FE (issue 3), "what upstream would accept" angle
2	
3	Written 2026-09-03 against worktree `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` at `45dab3be`
4	(FE = `experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks`, CN = `experimental/starrocks/src`,
5	proto = `experimental/starrocks/starrocks/gensrc/proto`). Evidence root = `scratchpad/perf/sf1000`.
6	Every number is **measured** (named evidence file or a command run for this design) or marked **inference**.
7	
8	## 0. Decision in one paragraph
9	
10	Give every FILES() scan the row count the system already knows, through the abstractions StarRocks already has for
11	stats-less tables, in two layers that share one FE code path:
12	
13	1. **Exact:** the CN already opens every parquet footer for the `get_file_schema` RPC (`file_schema.rs:19-25`); it
14	   returns the summed `FileMetaData::num_rows` in a new optional field of `PGetFileSchemaResult`
15	   (`internal_service.proto:647-650`). The FE stores it on `TableFunctionTable`.
16	2. **Fallback, FE-only:** when the field is absent (upstream BE, `fake://` in unit tests, non-parquet), the FE uses
17	   `total file bytes / sum(getTypeSize)` from the `TBrokerFileStatus.size` it already collected
18	   (`TableFunctionTable.java:611`), which is byte-for-byte the rule `HiveStatisticsProvider.getEstimatedRowCount`
19	   uses for Hive tables without statistics (`connector/hive/HiveStatisticsProvider.java:138-163`).
20	
21	`StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (`sql/optimizer/statistics/StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`) replaces
22	`setOutputRowCount(1)` with that estimate for `TableFunctionTable` scans. Column statistics stay `UNKNOWN` (no
23	min/max/NDV yet; that is a later layer). One mutable FE `Config` boolean, mirroring the existing Sirius FE knob
24	`files_query_whole_file_ranges` (`patches/files-query-whole-file-ranges.patch`), lets a reviewer flip old/new plans
25	with `ADMIN SET FRONTEND CONFIG` and `EXPLAIN COSTS` in minutes instead of a 40-minute FE rebuild.
26	
27	Delivered as two fork PRs on `experimental/starrocks` (the carve plan's layer for FE patches and CN code): PR-A = FE
28	patch + FE unit tests + doc rows + CI patch-apply generalisation; PR-B = proto field + CN + FE consumption + CN tests.
29	No engine (`src/`) change, no translator change.
30	
31	What this fix does **not** do, shown with the FE's own cost arithmetic in section 4: it does not by itself make
32	q05/q08/q09/q17/q18/q21 pass on 1 CN. The FE's cost model prefers shuffling a 6e9-row probe against any build above
33	~5M rows at 1 CN regardless of cardinalities, so lineitem still crosses an exchange until fix 4 (fusion or spill)
34	lands. Its value is that every downstream decision (build side, semi/anti commutation, broadcast guard, CTE reuse,
35	`broadcast_row_limit`, `exec_mem_limit`) stops being arithmetic on column widths (P3) and becomes tunable and
36	testable.

55	### 2.1 FE: `TableFunctionTable` owns the estimate

64	    return fileStatuses.stream().filter(f -> !f.isDir).mapToLong(f -> f.size).sum();

67	/** Row-count estimate for the CBO: footer total, else bytes / row width (Hive's rule), else 1. */
68	public long estimateRowCount() {
69	    if (!Config.files_scan_estimate_row_count) { return 1; }
70	    if (footerRowCount >= 0) { return Math.max(1, footerRowCount); }

155	    repeated PSlotDescriptor schema = 2;

280	### 4.2 The six 1-CN failures: the FE will still shuffle lineitem (inference, computed from the cost code)
281	
282	q05's lineitem join at 1 CN with exact counts. L = lineitem projection 6e9 rows x 28 B = 168 GB (measured parked
283	projection at death 171 GB, P1); R = customer x orders(0.25) = 3.75e8 rows x 12 B = 4.5 GB. `getRealCost`
284	weights 0.5/2/1.5 (`CostModel.java:129-135`):
285	
286	| term | BROADCAST R | SHUFFLE both |
287	|---|---:|---:|
288	| exchange (`visitPhysicalDistribution` :400-460; CN-only so `aliveBackendNumber = 0`, beNum 1; single registered node so shuffle network cost 0, `SystemInfoService.isSingleBackendAndComputeNode` :246-248) | 2R + 1.5R = 15.8, x1000 because 4.5 GB > `exec_mem_limit` 2 GiB (:426-428, `SessionVariable.DEFAULT_EXEC_MEM_LIMIT` :1305) = 15,750 | 0.5(L+R) = 86 |
289	| hash join (`HashJoinCostModel.getCpuCost/getMemCost/getAvgProbeCost` :85-157) | probe penalty min(12, ln(3.75e8/1e5)) = 8.2 -> 0.5(R + 8.2L) + 2R = 703 | penalty min(3, 8.2 - log2(parallelFactor)) = 3 -> 0.5(R + 3L) + 2R = 263 |
290	| total | 16,453 (718 even with the memory penalty removed) | 350 |
291	
292	SHUFFLE wins by 2x even with `exec_mem_limit` raised; broadcast wins at 1 CN only while ln(R_rows/1e5) < ~4, i.e.
293	build sides under ~5.5M rows (nation, region, supplier, filtered part). Each of the six has a lineitem join whose
294	other side is orders- or partsupp-derived (1e8-1e9 rows), so all six keep the P1 shape at 1 CN. With 4 registered
295	nodes (the survey condition, P3) shuffle network cost is nonzero and the margin narrows (345 vs 718 for the
296	exchanges) but the join penalty term still decides for shuffle. **Conclusion: fix 3 does not un-break the six; fix
297	4 does.** Fix 1 (fail fast) is what makes the still-wrong plans cheap to observe.
